Sounders FC vs. Colorado Rapids

Saturday, July 18, 2015

Kickoff: 7PM

Royal Brougham Park (CenturyLink Field)

Seattle, WA

By Chip Quinn

The guy driving the shuttle from the airport was on something. He had to be. There I was cursing my decision to bring a jacket, let alone wear a shirt, sweating near death like some Parisian in a freak heat wave, and this guy pokes a head skyward and comments on the coming snowstorm. A hallucinogen, no doubt. Or the legal weed was just that potent in Colorado. There was no snow. Not today. Not ever in this hellish climate.

So there I was the next day, calf deep in snow, steadying myself one-handed against Dick's Sporting Goods Park and trying to piss as the frigid breeze was making the task that much harder. I'd missed the game, obviously, but wanted to leave my comments on the Rapids performance as they dropped more points to the Sounders.

"Hey, I don't think you should be doing this," the cabbie hesitantly offered from within the still-running car.

"It's alright. It's Tuesday," I responded. That quieted him. Life tip: a factual non sequitur will often subdue the protests of most (it was Tuesday). Finishing the task I'd driven out to take care of, I returned to the car and headed back to the city. The cabbie and I didn't speak. There was no need. I'd said all I wanted to with regards to Colorado soccer.

Typically this would be the point I'd kick up my boots, crack a beer and wax poetic about 'easy points' from a bottom of the barrel team for our boys this Saturday. But we collectively did that this past weekend in Chicago against a worse side. And weeks before; against another dumpster fire team in Philly. The arrogance of drinking with feet crossed along the tabletop has cost us in points more than once this season. It's a wakeup call when our bell gets rung by teams tenuously hanging on the bottom one: there are no guaranteed wins in this sport.

There are points to keep in mind as we crowd into the Brougham End this weekend. Colorado has never won against Seattle in Seattle. Never. In fact, in every matchup between the Sounders and cRapids, they've only managed to sneak off with one win and a draw.The rest have been us. All us. While the boys in Rave Green have been stumbling some the Colorado kids have managed two wins in a row - their first this season. In fact, that doubles their wins for the whole season. Let that sink in.

The cRapids aren't good; they simply aren't. And they've never been their best (whatever that looks like) against the Sounders. This is no excuse to mellow our voices this Saturday. Those 3 points are ours: we have to take them. Sending Colorado back with nothing is a Seattle tradition; we need to get behind that in full force. There are some dark clouds stalking around our performance as of late. To deny that is a glitter job that serves no purpose. This game matters more than most, to correct this stumble back on course. To get behind the boys and mainline that enthusiasm back into them. That's what we do - and we've no equal in doing it in this league! I'm not one who really enjoys gritty, toe-to-toe battles of equally matched opponents. I like watching my team absolutely obliterate our enemies in cover-your-children's-eyes aggression. That's what Saturday will be for us. And we'll fill the city with our approval when the final whistle sounds and they're squeegeeing crimson-clad players from the turf.

I am a hereditary gardener. My dad started work as a landscaper, but ended up through the years working in a hospital. But he always loved to putter around outside, walking in a nearby conservation area or sitting on his balcony surrounded by planters. My mom could grow anything. I did not inherit her ability with indoor tropicals (unfortunately!) but I'm good with outdoor plants like she was. Even though we lived in a multi-story apartment building, my parents always surrounded themselves with outdoor plants.

Me? I have had plants in the ground or in planters since I moved away from home at 17. Even if it was just some inpatients in a window box on the fire escape, there was always something. I know that people think I'm super lucky to have my one acre property now with my perennial beds, but to be honest, I found it just as satisfying to sit in my small urban garden that was located right behind a busy plaza watching the butterflies and hummingbirds as I do sitting on my bigger porch that looks out over farmers fields. I truly believe that your home and happiness is what you make it....and as long as I had some place to sit outside, I am a happy camper.

I am always planning my next garden projects....next idea will be adding shrubs to the very front of our yard to try and hide the road a bit and also constructing a raised bed to start a vegetable patch. I've never been a big vegie gardener, but now that I have the space, I might give it a shot.

I have a very dear friend who thought she was a gardener too...she pictured herself as Mother Earth, growing organic vegies and herbs while tending her wee yard. But after several years it finally dawned on her that where I would come home from work and start weeding before I even changed out of my high heels and skirt, she would head inside and start mopping her floor. Her thing was inside, keeping a clean and wonderful indoors. Mine was outside.

So what is gardening about? Is it innate? Yup. It's part of who is am. It's actually how I describe myself to people. And even when I end up in a nursing home, I'll probably be doing something with soil.
